record.original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero and let I be a complete intersection ideal in the polynomial ring K[x1, ..., xn], where n is arbitrary. Must the Artinian quotient K[x1, ..., xn]/I always have the weak Lefschetz property, and does it perhaps always have the strong Lefschetz property as well?

evidence.quote: Question 2.1. Does every complete intersection ideal I ⊆ K[x1, . . . , xn], in any number of variables, has the WLP (or even the SLP)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $n \geq 1$, and let $R = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be the standard graded polynomial ring. An ideal $I \subseteq R$ is called a complete intersection if it is generated by a regular sequence of homogeneous polynomials $f_1, \ldots, f_c$ (so that $\mathrm{height}(I) = c$). The quotient $A = R/I$ is then a graded Artinian $K$-algebra, $A = \bigoplus_{d \geq 0} A_d$.

The algebra $A$ is said to have the Weak Lefschetz Property (WLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that, for every degree $d \geq 0$, the multiplication map
$$\times \ell : A_d \longrightarrow A_{d+1}$$
has maximal rank (i.e., is either injective or surjective).

The algebra $A$ is said to have the Strong Lefschetz Property (SLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that, for every $d \geq 0$ and every $k \geq 1$, the multiplication map
$$\times \ell^k : A_d \longrightarrow A_{d+k}$$
has maximal rank.

Question: Does every Artinian complete intersection quotient $K[x_1, \ldots, x_n]/I$ (with $K$ of characteristic zero and $n$ arbitrary) have the Weak Lefschetz Property? Does it always have the Strong Lefschetz Property?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a well-known longstanding open question in commutative algebra. WLP/SLP are known to hold for all complete intersections in codimension at most 3 (over a field of characteristic zero), but the general case remains open. Partial results are known for height-4 equigenerated complete intersections and for various special families (e.g., complete intersections of quadrics), but the full conjecture in arbitrary codimension is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A Tour of the Weak and Strong Lefschetz Properties (Migliore-Nagel survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing the WLP/SLP conjecture for complete intersections, with known results in codimensions 2 and 3 and open status in higher codimension.
status_evidence.claim: WLP for complete intersections is known up to codimension 3 in characteristic zero and is open in higher codimension.

status_evidence.title: On the weak Lefschetz property for height four equigenerated complete intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Recent partial results addressing WLP in codimension 4 for equigenerated complete intersections.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress is known in codimension 4.

status_evidence.title: Weak Lefschetz property of equigenerated complete intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper continuing investigations into WLP for higher-codimension equigenerated complete intersections, indicating the general question remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The general WLP question for complete intersections in arbitrary codimension is still open.
